title: Geometric decomposition of the $d$-dimensional hard-sphere partition function
abstract: We introduce a geometric decomposition of the hard-sphere partition function. Using a close-packing-inspired geometric bound on the available insertion volume, made rigorous when a corresponding local density certificate is available, we establish a reference upper bound $Q^\ast$ on the configurational integral. Factoring this upper bound out of the statistical geometric partition function of Speedy yields a new form for the $d$-dimensional partition function, $Q(N,V,T)=Q^\ast \exp(-N \mathcal{J})$, where $\mathcal{J}$ depends strictly on the boundary-to-volume ratio of the voids and the close-packing density. Overall, this work deepens our statistical geometric understanding of the hard-sphere system.
summary: This work introduces a novel geometric decomposition for calculating the hard-sphere partition function in $d$ dimensions. It factors the total partition function into an upper bound derived from close-packing geometry and an exponential penalty term related to void space fragmentation. This provides a powerful, geometrically controlled framework for understanding fluid thermodynamics across all densities.
main_problem: To derive a rigorous geometric decomposition for the $d$-dimensional hard-sphere partition function, $Q(N, V, T)$.
main_result: The partition function is shown to factorize into a reference upper bound ($Q^*$) and an exponential penalty term: $Q \propto Q^* \exp(-NJ)$, where $J$ depends on the boundary-to-volume ratio of voids.
method: The authors use geometric bounds, inspired by close-packing arguments and formalized via local density certificates (Blichfeldt-type), to establish an upper bound on the configurational integral.
model_or_system: The system is a classical hard-sphere fluid in $d$ dimensions. The analysis focuses on calculating the partition function based on the available insertion volume ($V_I$) for adding particles without overlap.
key_observables: Hard-sphere partition function ($Q$), Insertion Probability ($\Pi_I$), Packing Fraction ($\phi$), and Compressibility Factor ($Z$).
important_parameters: Dimensionality ($d$), Close-packing density ($\phi_{cp}$), and the ratio of surface area to volume of excluded regions.
main_assumptions: The rigorous derivation relies on the existence of a local density certificate that allows bounding the exclusion set volume, particularly at high densities.
figures_summary: Figures compare various bounds on the insertion probability ($\Pi_I$) against known exact solutions for low dimensions ($d=1$), and illustrate the decomposition of $Q$ into a reference bound ($Q^*$) and a geometric penalty factor.
paper_structure: The paper systematically develops the factorization, first establishing upper bounds using geometry (Chunk 1), then deriving the finite-$N$ exact relationship involving insertion volume ratios (Chunk 2), and finally confirming thermodynamic consistency across low-density (van der Waals) and high-density (close-packed limit) regimes (Chunks 3 & 4).
why_interesting: While focused on classical statistical mechanics, the rigorous geometric bounding techniques used to control fluctuations in the void space are highly relevant for developing controlled approximations in quantum many-body systems where local correlations dominate.
